A farmer plants saplings to replace trees felled for timber. The saplings grow independently of each other, and the farmer expects that 9% of those planted will be lost to disease, insects, and other causes.

(a) The farmer plants 20 saplings in a small field. For this plantation, determine

(i) the probability that 4 saplings will be lost. (2 marks)

(ii) the probability that more than one sapling will be lost. (1 mark)

(iii) the most likely number of saplings that will be lost. (1 mark)

(b) In a much larger field, 45 rows of 36 saplings are planted.

(i) Show that the probability that in one randomly chosen row no more than 3 saplings will be lost is 0.5912. (2 marks)

(ii) Determine the probability that less than half of the rows will lose no more than
3 saplings. (2 marks)

The game consists of three 8-sided dice, numbered 1 to 8, each placed in a cup. The cup is shaken, the dice rolled, and the number of sevens are recorded.

Let X be a random variable denoting the number of sevens rolled in a Triple Roll game.

x 0 1 2 3

Each player pays $2 to play Triple Roll game. If a player rolls one 7 they win $2, if they roll two 7s, they win $4 and if they roll three 7s they win $7.

  1. Determine the school’s expected profit/loss for each game of Triple Roll. (3 marks)

  2. Determine the probability that a player will make a profit in a game of Triple Roll. (2 marks)

Year 12 students want to increase the attraction of the game by providing the opportunity for larger winnings. They modify the rules of the game so that players only win money when two or more 7s are rolled and the winnings for rolling three 7s is five times as much as the winning for rolling of two 7s. Each game still costs $2 to play. Year 12 students estimated that they should be able to run 300 games and wants to make profit of $200 for the school.

  1. Determine the winnings Year 12 students should set for rolling three 7s with the modifications above. (3 marks)

(2 marks) Year 12 students want to increase the attraction of the game by providing the opportunity for larger winnings. They modify the rules of the game so that players only win money when two or more 7s are rolled and the winnings for rolling three 7s is five times as much as the winning for rolling of two 7s. Each game still costs $2 to play. Year 12 students estimated that they should be able to run 300 games and wants to make profit of $200 for the school. Determine the winnings Year 12 students should set for rolling three 7s with the modifications above. (3 marks)
